https://musicbrainz.org/doc/Style/Recording#Numb…
Number of audio channels
It may be the case that very similar released tracks have different numbers of audio channels. The most common audio channel configuration is stereo (two channels; left and right). However, there are several common audio channel configurations used in recordings, including mono (one channel), quadraphonic (four channels) and surround sound (various multi-channel configurations).
These different configurations should generally be distinguished by using separate recordings. However, the original multi-channel recording should be used when multiple channels have been combined into a single channel without actually creating a new mix from the source audio tracks. A similar exception should be made where a mono channel has been split into two stereo channels - for example, in Duophonic recordings.

#68713785Edit mediumtillywilly2020-04-08 00:19 GMT+2👍 yes

2020-04-08 00:19 GMT+2

You Mean So Much to Me and The Fever were gifted from Bruce to Southside for his first album with a ribbon and bow
How many times has Bruce sung You Mean So Much to Me since then? My guess is twice May 12-13 1977 when he filled in for Southside
Hearts of Stone and Talk to Me were demoed with the E Street Band October 14, 1977; Iovine prepared a cassette and gave it to Miami Steve, their mgr and producer
when sessions started, he loaned Max Weinberg to SSJ for the album
Little Girl of Mine was a song he was wriiting 1976, he and Sugar Miami worked it into Little Girl So Fine Dec 1976, and wrote Love on the Wrong Side of Town, Bruce also let Steve use When You Dance, which they also wrote together in 1971
Out of all these, the only song he played was "The Fever" Read Brucebase. I wrote that whole section
If I may quote myself
"After they left Texas, "The Fever" was not played again until they returned on July 14, 1978 to San Antonio. Springsteen has said he never liked "The Fever", but played it on the Darkness tour in many cities because, "people would jump onstage and grab me by the head and scream, ‘Bruce! Fever!" It was played at Sam Houston Coliseum in Houston the next evening, and twenty-two more times to the end of the Darkness tour, including twelve just in December. Though he joined Southside Johnny for duets many times, and it was rehearsed during soundchecks for the 1999-2000 Reunion tour, it was not performed again until September 24, 1999 in Philadelphia, PA. "
The other songs I mentioned he never plays except occasional Talk to Me
These are not "Cover songs" Maybe when Bruce performs them, he is covering SSJ. Same for I Don't Want to Go Home and the songs Steve wrote when he was with the Jukes. When he put them on archival compilations to present the grand picture of his career, or played three in 2017, he was not taking them back.
Just count the numbers. the numbers the numbers the numbers they tell the story
Southside has performed The Fever and I Don't Want to Go Home over 1,000 times each (I'm not looking it up, you guys can google). Bruce and Steve ... look it up

#68177115Merge release groupstigerman3252020-03-22 17:46 GMT+1👎 no

tigerman325
2020-03-22 17:46 GMT+1

A single doesn't have 5 different tracks unless they are remixes of the same basic track. Look at the Beatles, etc. There are tons of examples in which there was an EP version released in UK and a single version released at the same time that only had 2 tracks. A single can be more than 2 tracks if they all have the same basic recording, Your example of the remixes points this out. The EP you are merging to the single has 5 unique tracks. That is a textbook example of an EP. Now, I personally thank all remix singles should be different from basic singles, but that's a whole other discussion that is more controversial than this one.
https://musicbrainz.org/doc/Release_Group/Type
It's possible to make the argument that is's a maxi-single I suppose, but I never really thought those were prevalent until CD single releases.
https://musicbrainz.org/doc/Style/Release_Group
Other situations
There are a number of situations where there is currently no consensus about whether releases should be grouped together or not. This includes the same album sung in different languages, re-recorded albums and remixed albums. Be aware that attempting to group these releases can be quite controversial. If in doubt, these releases should probably be in separate release groups.
Discogs always groups EP & Singles together, MB doesn't.

As far as I can tell all of the sleeves, covers and other package contents are the same... except for the actual discs. The numbers on the discs and packaging are all the same
Your CDs say:
ALL RIGHTS RESERVED. MADE IN THE EU. BIEM/GEMA. LC 00162
Mine say:
"COLUMBIA" AND <COLUMBIA LOGO?> REG. U.S. PAT. & TM. OFF. MARCA REGISTRADA.
So, yours looks like an EU release. Mine looks like a US release or a "rest of the world other than EU" release. Who can tell? :-)
Blu-ray discs are the same except mine add the above text about Columbia and don't have the "Sony Music", "U" or "FSK ab 0 freigegeben" logos. Wow, the last of these really does suggest a German release, rather than a generic EU one.
